Saves the raw recording for each dictation as a WAV file so you can replay it from the chat tab. Only the 5 most recent recordings are kept; older ones are deleted automatically to cap disk usage. Stays on this phone — nothing is uploaded. Off by default since audio is more sensitive than the transcript.
Removes every recording on this phone. Play buttons on past conversations disappear; the capture toggle stays where it is.

Core Devices (formerly rePebble) handles watch dictation itself via a configurable pipeline (local, cloud, or a mix; picker inside Core Devices\' settings). Wristotle\'s on-device Whisper isn\'t used for what you say into your watch. Other Wristotle features (Calls, SMS, Reminders, Open/Play app) still work normally.

If you want on-device transcription via Wristotle\'s Whisper, switch your BLE companion to microPebble — it routes dictation through Android\'s speech recognizer, which Wristotle can intercept with Whisper.
Talk to your watch and the history will show up here.
This permanently removes every saved interaction. The 30-day window will start fresh.
Required to look up contacts by name
Required to answer calendar questions and create events ("when is my next meeting", "schedule a meeting tomorrow at 3pm")
Required to dial from the watch
Required to text from the watch
Keeps the watch bridge alive in the background
Active — Wristotle can control media apps
Not granted — say \"play\" / \"pause\" / \"next\" won\'t do anything yet

Lets the watch control any media app on this phone — \"play\", \"pause\", \"next\", \"previous\", \"rewind ten seconds\", \"play YouTube\", \"pause Spotify\". Android calls this Notification Access; it\'s the system gate that lets one app see active media sessions. Grant it once and the watch can drive playback in any installed media app.
This device doesn\'t expose the Notification Access page in Settings.
Granted — \"what\'s the weather\" answers for your current location
Not granted — bare \"what\'s the weather\" replies with a hint; \"weather in <city>\" still works

Coarse (~3 km) location lets the bare \"what\'s the weather\" voice command read your phone\'s last-known location and report the conditions there. Optional — without it, ask \"weather in <city>\" instead. No background location is used; the handler reads the cached fix at the moment you ask.
Active — \"open <app>\" from the watch foregrounds reliably
Not granted — \"open <app>\" from the watch may not foreground when the app isn\'t in a recent state

Without this grant, Android 14+ silently blocks Wristotle from foregrounding a different app when triggered by a watch dictation (the background-launch restriction). \"open Spotify\" / \"open Maps\" / etc. will appear to succeed but the target app stays in the background. Granting \"Display over other apps\" to Wristotle adds it to Android\'s background-launch allow-list and the foregrounding works reliably. Wristotle never actually draws anything on top of other apps — only the grant matters.\n\nLimits to be honest about: this fixes \"open <app>\" cold-start. It does NOT fix \"play <app>\" auto-resume — the play step depends on the target app accepting commands from a sideloaded caller, and most major media apps (Spotify, Tempo, etc.) only accept Google Assistant. \"play <app>\" will still open the app reliably, but starting playback may require a tap.
This device doesn\'t expose the \"Display over other apps\" page in Settings.

Registers Wristotle\'s on-device Whisper as Android\'s default speech recognition service. In principle any app that calls `android.speech.SpeechRecognizer` would then transcribe through Wristotle — though we haven\'t verified which third-party apps actually use that API in practice (many bundle their own engine). Enable via the picker below or via the ADB command.

Doesn\'t affect your watch — Core Devices (formerly rePebble) handles dictation itself with a configurable pipeline (local, cloud, or a mix; picker inside Core Devices\' settings). The setup below would register Wristotle as Android\'s default speech recognition service; in principle any app that calls Android\'s `SpeechRecognizer` API would transcribe through Wristotle\'s Whisper, but we haven\'t verified which third-party apps actually use that API.
Active — Wristotle is the system voice input provider
Not set as the default voice input
Command copied. Run it from a computer with ADB connected to this device.
Run the copied command from a computer connected to this device over ADB.
Most devices land in the Digital Assistant picker, where Wristotle won\'t appear. Use the ADB option if that happens.
This device doesn\'t expose a voice-input picker in Settings. Use the ADB command instead.

Choose how dictation is transcribed. Local Whisper runs entirely on this phone and works offline. Cloud / self-hosted endpoints accept any OpenAI-compatible /audio/transcriptions URL — Groq, OpenAI, Cloudflare Workers AI, a Speaches or whisper.cpp HTTP server on your homelab, etc. Picking a primary + fallback lets the other side step in if the first one fails.
Includes the /v1 suffix on most providers. /audio/transcriptions is appended automatically.

Compatible with any provider that exposes OpenAI\'s /audio/transcriptions shape — OpenAI, Groq, Cloudflare Workers AI, Together AI, a Speaches or whisper.cpp HTTP server on your homelab, LiteLLM/LocalAI proxies, …
Leave blank for self-hosted servers behind a Tailnet without auth. Sent as a Bearer header.

Downloads a Whisper speech recognition model that runs entirely on this device — no audio is sent to the cloud. Larger models are more accurate but slower; tiny.en is the fastest for short watch commands while base.en handles longer dictation better. Tap any downloaded model to make it the active one.

Core Devices (formerly rePebble) handles watch dictation itself via a configurable pipeline (local, cloud, or a mix; picker inside Core Devices\' settings), so a downloaded Whisper model here has no effect on your watch. It would only matter if you set Wristotle as Android\'s default speech recognition service and an app on your phone called the standard `SpeechRecognizer` API — a path we haven\'t verified end-to-end.

If you want on-device transcription for your watch via Wristotle\'s Whisper, switch your BLE companion app to microPebble — it routes dictation through Android\'s speech recognizer, which Wristotle\'s Whisper can take over.

Pick a `.bin` whisper.cpp model from anywhere on your phone — useful for fine-tuned, language-specific, or distilled variants that aren\'t in the list above. The first four bytes are checked for the ggml/GGUF header before the file is copied in.

Pin a spoken phrase to a specific app — useful when dictation mishears the app name ("adobe" for Audible), you prefer a nickname ("podcasts" for Pocket Casts), or the launcher label is awkward to say.

How to add one:
1. Tap "+ Add alias" and type the phrase exactly as you'd say it (lowercase, no punctuation; spaces are fine).
2. Pick the target app from the search list.
3. Save. The next "open \<phrase\>" / "launch \<phrase\>" voice command opens that app.

Aliases win over the normal name matching. Compound words are tolerated automatically — an alias stored as "audiobook" still matches when dictation transcribes "audio book" (and vice versa), so you don't need to add both spellings.
No aliases yet. Add one below to fix a misheard or nicknamed app.

Pin a spoken phrase to a specific contact, for when dictation mishears a name (\"next\" for \"text\" puts the wrong word in the contact slot) or you use a nickname (\"partner\" → a specific stored contact). Aliases win over the normal contact matching.
No aliases yet. Add one below to fix a misheard or nicknamed contact.
Grant Contacts access in Permissions to add aliases.
This phrase already matches %1$s — your alias will override that.
Get the most out of Wristotle. Each step is optional; you can come back here any time. We only list what\'s left to do — finished steps disappear from this list automatically.
✓ You\'re all set up. Anything you change later that needs attention will reappear here.
Wristotle transcribes watch dictation locally with whisper.cpp. Pick a Fast / Balanced / Accurate model in Settings → Models. Free, no account, no audio leaves your phone.

~23 MB MiniLM model that lets Wristotle recognise paraphrased commands (\"text mom on my way\" / \"shoot mom a quick message\"). Without it only the canonical openers (call/text/remind/open/play/…) match.

Wristotle needs Contacts, SMS, Phone, and Microphone permission to call, text, and transcribe. Each is asked for the first time you use the relevant feature, but granting them upfront avoids interruptions.
Builds the local index Wristotle uses to resolve \"open Spotify\" → the actual package. Runs once; re-runs are quick. Lives in Settings → Learning → Installed apps.
Map common mishears (\"call mum\" → Mom, \"text JK\" → John Kennedy) so Wristotle doesn\'t guess wrong. One-tap to add via Settings → Learning → Contact aliases.
Same shape as contact aliases but for apps — \"play music\" → Spotify, \"open the bank\" → your specific banking app. Optional. Settings → Learning → App aliases.

Optional: point Wristotle at an OpenAI-compatible /audio/transcriptions endpoint (Groq, OpenAI, self-hosted Speaches, …) for sub-second cloud transcription. Local Whisper stays available as a fallback.
Bring-your-own LLM key to enable \"ask agent <question>\" / \"ask claude <question>\" on the watch. Anthropic, OpenAI, OpenRouter, Ollama, llama.cpp — any provider with a Chat Completions endpoint.
Wristotle works on a fresh install, but a few one-time setup steps unlock the full experience — local speech transcription, paraphrase recognition, contact lookups, and app launching by name.
We\'ll walk through %1$d short step(s). Skip any time.
Everything\'s already set up — nothing to do. Tap below to dismiss.
Anything you skipped is still available under Settings → 🌟 Setup. Voice commands work right away — try \"call Mom\" or \"what\'s the weather\".
You can re-run this walkthrough from Settings → 🌟 Setup → Show welcome again.
The welcome walkthrough will appear the next time you open Wristotle. You can skip it again from there.

Create one-shot alarms that ring on the phone, the watch, or both. The watch leg can be cancelled with the voice command "cancel alarm". Phone alarms have to be dismissed in the phone\'s clock app — Android doesn\'t expose an API to cancel them.
No alarms yet — tap + Add alarm to create one.
Ask about games by voice — next fixture, last result, live score, and league standings. Save favorite teams so \"did we win?\" works without naming a team.

Picks the unit and the backend for voice weather queries. Default is open-meteo (no key, free). Switch to OpenWeather if you\'d rather use your own free-tier API key — more control over your quota and slightly different data fields.
Get a free key at openweathermap.org → API keys. Stored locally; sent only with weather requests to OpenWeather.
Quick tips for features you might not stumble onto by tapping around, and a running list of everything Wristotle does — newest first, with the release it shipped in.
Newest releases at the top. Each entry shows the version + release date, what it does, and where useful a sample voice command.
No tips or features match that search.
Stuck? The troubleshooting page covers dictation problems, permissions, the Whisper hallucination filter, and more.

Routes the "ask agent …" / "ask claude …" voice intent to an LLM. Phase B1 is plain Q&A only — MCP tool calling (so the LLM can actually take actions) lands in phase B2. Pick a provider, paste your API key, and the next voice query goes through.
How many recent turns are resent so follow-ups (\"and tomorrow?\") have context. Keep it small — history costs speed on the watch.
Clear the conversation after this long with no use, e.g. 300 = 5 minutes. 0 = never.
Say one of these to start a fresh conversation. One per line.
Extra HTTP headers sent with each request, one \"Name: Value\" per line. For server-side sessions and similar.
Off — reach the agent with a wake word (default)
Send unrecognised speech to Ask Agent
Ask Agent only — send every command, no wake word

Fallback keeps phone commands (call, text, timers, notes) and routes anything unmatched to the agent. Ask Agent only skips phone commands and sends every spoken command straight to the agent. Both need a provider configured below.
Get a key at console.anthropic.com → API Keys. Stored locally; sent only with AskAgent requests.
Lets Claude search the web mid-reply for fresh facts (news, sports, weather, today\'s prices). Billed by Anthropic at $10 per 1,000 searches on top of normal token costs. Off by default.
API key (leave blank for local servers)

Sent with every AskAgent query. Pre-populated with a watch-friendly baseline that keeps responses short + plain-text. Edit freely; clear it entirely to send NO system prompt (the LLM may produce verbose markdown the watch can\'t render).\n\nUsing a reasoning model (Qwen3 / DeepSeek-R1 / QwQ)? Configure your inference server (e.g. vLLM\'s --enable-reasoning --reasoning-parser flag) to move the <think> chain-of-thought out of the response — see the Troubleshooting page.

Extra wake words for the agent. One per line, or separated by commas. Use them either as wake words (\"Jarvis, what\'s the weather?\") or with a verb (\"ask jarvis …\"). Built-ins (agent, claude, ai, …) only work with a verb — \"agent\" alone is too generic to bare-match safely.
How long to wait for the agent to reply. Raise this for slow local models that \"think\" before answering (e.g. 120). Range 5–300; default 14.

Forwards a spoken command to your self-hosted Home Assistant and speaks back its reply. Say \"hey home assistant …\" (or just \"home assistant …\") and the rest is sent to HA\'s conversation agent — HA does the rest. Companion-local; nothing leaves your device except the command text to your own server.
Your HA address, e.g. http://homeassistant.local:8123 or https://<your-domain>. LAN / Tailscale / self-signed http:// all work. No trailing path — /api/conversation/process is added for you.
In HA: your profile → Security → Long-lived access tokens → Create. Stored locally; sent only with Home Assistant requests.
Extra wake words on top of the built-ins (home assistant, hass). One per line, or separated by commas. Use them as wake words (\"Jarvis, turn off the lights\") or with a verb (\"tell jarvis to …\").
⚠ \"%1$s\" also triggers Ask Agent. It will route to Home Assistant.
How long to wait for Home Assistant to reply. Range 5–120; default 10.

Phase A — add HTTP MCP servers and inspect their tools. The AskAgent voice intent that uses these is coming in phase B. Tool calls here are for debug verification only; pick an LLM-side dialogue later.
The Authorization value will be sent as-is. Most MCP servers expect a scheme prefix like \"Bearer <token>\" — without it the server will likely return 401 Unauthorized.\n\nSave anyway?
Tap 🔄 to load this server\'s tools.

Defaults for reminder voice commands. Used when the transcription is missing a piece of information the handler needs to fill in.
Reminders you ask for with "persistent reminder", "nag me", or "keep reminding me" also fire a phone notification at intervals after the watch pin goes off, until you tap Stop.

Stored in plaintext unless you set a password below.
App preferences (Notes / Conversation / NLU / Diagnostics / Reminder / active model)
Ask Agent setup (provider + model + system prompt)
Home Assistant setup (URL + language + wake words)
TTS provider setup (mode + endpoint + model + voice + per-intent toggles)

You selected secret categories (API keys / auth headers) but didn\'t set a password. The ZIP will be plaintext — anyone who opens it can read the tokens.\n\nProceed anyway, or cancel to add a password?
Say \"note: …\" or \"make a note that …\" on your watch.
This permanently deletes every saved note and its recording. This cannot be undone.
How many notes to keep. \"All\" never deletes; the other options FIFO-prune oldest notes (and their recordings) when the cap is reached.
How the new dictation\'s audio is stored on the note.
Delete the file when the entry is removed
Sync is disabled or no folder picked.

Write every note as a file in a folder you pick on this device — works with Obsidian vaults, Joplin/Logseq watch folders, Dropbox/Google Drive sync roots, git-versioned vaults, or any plain-text app. Markdown by default; the file format stays CommonMark-clean so it round-trips across every tool.

How to enable:
1. Flip the toggle below.
2. Tap "Pick folder" and choose the destination (e.g. your Obsidian vault).
3. Optional: change format / granularity / delete behaviour.

Notes write to "Wristotle/notes/" inside the picked folder; audio recordings go to "Wristotle/notes/attachments/". Cloud distribution is the picked folder's job — if you pick a folder inside Dropbox, Dropbox syncs it.

Write every voice query + response to a folder you pick on this device. Same architecture as the Notes sync card (any Obsidian / Joplin / Logseq vault, any Dropbox / Drive / Syncthing folder, any plain-text app — Wristotle writes; your existing sync stack distributes). Default granularity is \"Append to single file\" because per-query files would flood the vault.\n\nEverything goes under \"Wristotle/conversations/\" in the picked folder — \"conversations.md\" (append mode) or one \"<timestamp>.md\" per entry, with audio recordings (when captured) in \"attachments/\".
Type, or tap the mic to dictate
Live mirror of the settings stored on the Pebble. Changes are sent to the watch when you tap Save.
Keep the Wristotle app open on your watch while loading or saving — Pebble only syncs with the app that\'s currently running.
Tap Refresh to load settings from the watch.
Couldn\'t reach the watch. Make sure it\'s connected and the Wristotle watch app is running.
The Wristotle watch app needs an update to manage settings from here. Install the latest .pbw on the watch and tap Refresh.
Lights up icons, the menu highlight, and the chat progress strip in color. No effect on black-and-white watches.
Skip system retry dialog on dictation error
Each button on the chat surface opens one of: Dictation (start speaking), Quick menu (chooser), Notes, or Tasks.

Bundles app version, device info, granted permissions, active models, the installed-app index summary, recent conversation rows, and the last ~200 lines of in-app logs into a markdown report you can paste into a Codeberg issue. Stays entirely on this phone until you submit it. Redact contact names + phone numbers by default; flip the toggle off only if you understand what you\'re sharing.
Redact contact names + numbers + message bodies
Conversation rows are fully blanked; log lines only strip phone-digit runs — contact names and spoken text inside log routing decisions may still appear. Review the clipboard before submitting.
Include last 3 dictation audio files (attach manually)
Diagnostics copied to clipboard — paste into the issue body.

Scans this phone\'s installed apps so the watch can open or play them by name — \"open Spotify\", \"play Audible\", \"launch Maps\". The index is stored locally on this phone and is only refreshed when you tap below; re-scan whenever you install or uninstall an app so the watch knows about it.

Optional sentence encoder (~23 MB) so the watch understands commands phrased naturally — \"ring Mom\", \"tell Dad I\'ll be late\", \"buzz me at three\" — instead of the literal verb-first patterns. Without it, the watch falls back to prefix matching, which works for \"call Mom\" or \"text Dad …\" but misses paraphrases.

When on, every successful command is added to the intent classifier\'s example bank so similar phrasings are recognized more confidently next time. Learned examples stay on this phone — nothing leaves the device — and can be cleared anytime with the button below.
Removes everything Wristotle has learned from your past commands. The seed examples bundled with the app stay.
These phrases were captured from your successful commands and stay on this phone. Delete any you\'d rather Wristotle forget.
Add one above, or say \"add task <…>\" to your watch.
Permanently removes every task — pending and completed.
Voice "morning brief" reads back today\'s meetings, alarms, reminders, tasks, notes, and unread messages.

By default the brief only shows messages currently sitting in your tray. Turn this on to also include notifications you swiped or cleared earlier today. Wristotle records app id + conversation key + timestamp only — never the body, title, or sender of a notification.
